channel.title: CyberView: high-priority cyber events
channel.description: High-severity incidents, exploited vulnerabilities and urgent advisories from CyberView, with what to do, researched and written by CyberView AI (a Claude model). Unverified claims are left out.

item.title: Exploit code published for Microsoft Defender privilege-escalation flaw CVE-2026-33825, fixed in April 2026
item.description:
ScanNetSecurity reports that exploit code has been published for CVE-2026-33825, a privilege-escalation flaw in the Microsoft Defender Antimalware Platform that Microsoft fixed in April 2026. Cybersecurity.com says an attacker who already has a foothold could chain it to take full control of a host. ScanNetSecurity advises applying the security update.
What to do: ScanNetSecurity advises applying the security update that fixes the flaw.
CVEs: CVE-2026-33825 (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: CISA adds ten exploited flaws to KEV: Mitel MiCollab, Vates Xen Orchestra, Juniper Session Smart, Danfoss AK-SM 800A
item.description:
CISA's catalog lists ten additions dated 25 November: five in Mitel MiCollab, one in Vates Xen Orchestra, one in HPE Juniper Session Smart, three in Danfoss AK-SM 800A. Federal due dates are 28 November for eight and 9 December for two. Daily Security Review reports that Accenture Apex Labs says the Mitel flaws were exploited as zero-days in a suspected extortion campaign.
What to do: CISA's catalog entries say to apply vendor mitigations as BOD 26-04 requires, or stop using the product if none are available; Mitel advises its fixed MiCollab release and restricting external access to the conferencing component, per Infobae.
CVEs: CVE-2026-103406, CVE-2026-133469, CVE-2025-41450, CVE-2023-25914, CVE-2023-25915, CVE-2026-133324, CVE-2026-133275, CVE-2026-133311, CVE-2026-133303, CVE-2026-133323 (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: Swiss cyber office BACS reports first AI-agent-assisted attacks on companies in Switzerland
item.description:
Switzerland's Federal Office for Cybersecurity (BACS) reports its first attacks assisted by AI agents, Inside-IT says. Datensicherheit.de, citing Swiss media, says BACS learned of five incidents, four with a successful intrusion, affecting three critical-infrastructure companies and two SMEs. No major outages have been reported so far, according to that article. BACS urges installing critical updates quickly.
What to do: BACS advises installing critical security updates for internet-facing systems within 24 hours at the latest. (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: Switzerland's BACS says five cyberattacks used AI agents, four compromised systems, per Reuters and The420
item.description:
Switzerland's Federal Office for Cybersecurity (BACS) said five cyberattacks in the past few days used AI agents against companies and critical infrastructure operators, Reuters reports. Four of the five compromised computer systems. Three targets were critical infrastructure operators, which Swiss broadcaster SRF said were electricity, water and telecommunications providers. BACS did not say who was behind the attacks.
What to do: The Swiss National Cyber Security Centre, per The420, recommends reducing the number of systems directly reachable from the internet and protecting remote access with multi-factor authentication or passkeys. (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: Hunt.io reports an intrusion crew's exposed files show credential attacks on US law firms; no breach of any firm found
item.description:
Hunt.io says open web directories left by an unnamed crew held target lists, scan results, logs and malware, with law firms, federal agencies, a hospital system and a manufacturer targeted. It says Simpson Thacher & Bartlett was under sustained credential attack and that CVE-2019-19781 was tried against Citrix gateways, but every captured result showed failure. Hunt.io says named is not breached; Cyber Press relays the findings.
What to do: Hunt.io advises requiring MFA on VPN and Citrix gateways, patching the listed CVEs, removing management interfaces from the internet and alerting on credential-stuffing patterns.
CVEs: CVE-2019-19781 (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: NSFOCUS: new VeilDHT botnet spreads to Linux servers and IoT devices
item.description:
NSFOCUS's risk alert describes VeilDHT, a previously unseen botnet it says mainly targets Linux servers and IoT devices. NSFOCUS says it spreads by exploiting flaws including CVE-2024-3912 (ASUS routers) and CVE-2021-35394 (Realtek Jungle SDK), can run DDoS attacks and commands, and hides a backup C2 channel in a public P2P network. CNCERT observed as many as 15,805 active bots in a single day, with a cumulative total of 40,467 infected devices.
What to do: NSFOCUS advises keeping an up-to-date asset inventory, patching known vulnerabilities including IoT firmware, monitoring DNS and IP activity tied to its IOCs, and isolating and remediating any infected host.
CVEs: CVE-2024-3912, CVE-2021-35394 (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: Drupal says core access-bypass flaw CVE-2026-136716 (SA-CORE-2026-019) is being exploited in the wild
item.description:
Drupal's advisory SA-CORE-2026-019 rates the access bypass in Drupal core, CVE-2026-136716, highly critical and says it is being exploited in the wild. It follows SA-CORE-2026-017, and Drupal says any site that left its installer remotely accessible following that advisory may still have been compromised. Fixes are in 10.6.23, 11.3.23 and 11.4.14. HKCERT rates it high.
What to do: Drupal advises updating to the fixed version for your release line and running update.php, securing the installer, and checking logs for unauthorized access, especially to the user 1 account.
CVEs: CVE-2026-136716 (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: Swiss NCSC reports first cyberattacks on Swiss organisations carried out with AI agents
item.description:
Switzerland's NCSC says it has received its first reports of cyberattacks on organisations in Switzerland carried out with AI agents; several organisations and critical infrastructure operators in at least two sectors were affected. The NCSC says that in every attack it knows of, the agents led to a successful compromise of the victims' IT systems. It names no victims and gives no total.
What to do: The NCSC advises limiting internet-facing systems, installing critical updates on them without delay, requiring MFA or passkeys for internet-accessible resources such as webmail and VPNs, and using least privilege and regular testing. (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: F5 Labs: honeynet recorded 46 exploitation attempts against Ivanti Connect Secure CVE-2026-104935
item.description:
F5 Labs says its honeynet sensors recorded 46 exploitation attempts matching CVE-2026-104935, an authentication bypass in Ivanti Connect Secure, from 4 distinct source IPs on October 26 and 27. F5 describes broad multi-exploit scanners, not targeted exploitation of a single victim. It says the CVE was added to CISA's KEV catalog on October 13, 2026, and that six public proof-of-concept exploits are tracked.
What to do: F5 Labs advises to patch now and apply Ivanti's fixed versions; per Ivanti's advisory data the flaw is fixed in ICS 25.1.3.0.
CVEs: CVE-2026-104935 (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: Patchstack: WP Rocket plugin before 3.24.2 unauthenticated RCE (CVE-2026-125812) is being exploited in the wild
item.description:
Patchstack says WP Rocket versions before 3.24.2 have an unauthenticated remote code execution flaw, CVE-2026-125812, rated CVSS 9.8, and that it is currently being targeted in the wild; it says its first observed attempt was on 25 November. Patchstack says only sites with LazyLoad for CSS background images or Host Fonts Locally enabled are affected. Zeropath says WP Media fixed it in 3.24.2.
What to do: Patchstack advises updating to 3.24.2 or later; it says the update does not remove files already planted, and that sites unable to update can disable both affected features or use its mitigation rule.
CVEs: CVE-2026-125812 (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: VirtueMart extension for Joomla: unauthenticated file inclusion flaw (CVE-2026-133335), exploited in the wild per CVE record
item.description:
The CVE record for CVE-2026-133335, assigned by Joomla, describes an unauthenticated local file inclusion in the main controller of the VirtueMart extension for Joomla, versions 4.0.0 through 4.8.7, which depending on the server could lead to remote code execution. The record says it is fixed in 4.8.8 and that the issue has been exploited in the wild. CVSS 4.0 score: 9.2.
What to do: Update the VirtueMart extension to 4.8.8, the version the CVE record says fixes the flaw.
CVEs: CVE-2026-133335 (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: ThreatDown says Booba ransomware hit an East Coast US water plant network and reached the local government network that oversees it
item.description:
Malwarebytes ThreatDown says a ransomware attack began on the network of an East Coast water treatment plant in November 2026 and reached the network of the local government that oversees it. ThreatDown says its managed detection and response team contained it three machines past the line where its coverage began; the plant side was run by a separate provider without ThreatDown oversight. It names the ransomware as Booba; the victims are not named.
What to do: ThreatDown advises knowing exactly where your security coverage ends and not reconnecting machines until the whole network is verified clean. (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: GeoServer: watchTowr reports exploitation of two flaws; researchers describe unauthenticated RCE chain
item.description:
The Hacker News says watchTowr reports exploitation of CVE-2026-120705 (an arbitrary file read) and a second flaw: its list names CVE-2026-129243, but a watchTowr quote names CVE-2026-129244. GovCERT.HK says reports indicate CVE-2026-120705 and CVE-2026-129243 are exploited in the wild. Eye Security describes an unauthenticated RCE chain needing no special settings. Fixes are in 3.0.2, 2.28.6 and 2.27.7.
What to do: GovCERT.HK advises taking immediate action to mitigate the risk and says patches are available; The Hacker News names fixes 2.27.7, 2.28.6 and 3.0.2.
CVEs: CVE-2026-120705, CVE-2026-129243, CVE-2026-129245, CVE-2026-120704 (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: Barracuda says two flaws in Email Security Gateway and other products are exploited against a small number of organizations
item.description:
Barracuda says it has identified exploitation activity affecting a small number of organizations, per BleepingComputer. The flaws are CVE-2026-116606, an authentication bypass in Email Security Gateway, and CVE-2026-111560, a command injection that also affects five other products. Barracuda says that combined they could allow root access. Security-Insider reports the vendor advises restricting admin interfaces to trusted internal networks.
What to do: Barracuda advises customers to manually apply the appropriate patch as soon as possible, enable automatic patching if disabled, and restrict admin interface access to trusted internal networks.
CVEs: CVE-2026-116606, CVE-2026-111560 (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: Palo Alto Networks says CVE-2026-46300 (Fragnesia) exploited against internet-exposed PAN-OS management interfaces
item.description:
Palo Alto Networks bulletin PAN-SA-2026-0015 says exploitation has been observed of CVE-2026-46300, a Linux kernel local privilege escalation flaw named Fragnesia, targeting the PAN-OS management interface exposed to the internet. The vendor says the known path first requires exploiting PHP2Shell and that it is not aware of any other exploitation method. The bulletin is rated informational; fixed PAN-OS builds are listed.
What to do: Palo Alto Networks advises: if a management interface is reachable from the internet, upgrade immediately (for example to 12.2.4-h3, 11.2.16-h3, 11.1.16-h6 or 10.2.18-h15) and restrict access to trusted internal IP addresses; otherwise upgrade at the next maintenance interval.
CVEs: CVE-2026-46300 (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: HoneyLabs reports exploit attempts against exposed Vite dev servers, targeting advisory GHSA-p4f5-76q4-ffq7
item.description:
HoneyLabs says its honeypots recorded exploit attempts from 15 November against Vite dev servers exposed with --host or server.host, aimed at advisory GHSA-p4f5-76q4-ffq7. According to HoneyLabs the payloads search for .env files, AWS credentials and API keys; its honeypots had no Vite behind them, so nothing ran. SecurityOnline reports the advisory scores 9.1 on CVSS v4.0 and that a working PoC is public in it.
What to do: HoneyLabs advises patching Vite (6.4.6, 7.3.8, 8.1.7, 8.2.5 or 8.3.7) and not exposing dev servers to the network; SecurityOnline advises removing the --host flag. (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: 3CX tells self-managed customers to update to V20 Update 10 for two NGINX HTTP/2 vulnerabilities
item.description:
3CX's advisory says two NGINX HTTP/2 vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-123633, CVE-2026-123007) affect self-managed 3CX systems; the fix is V20 Update 10, Build 20.0.10.1801. 3CX says hosted and SMB systems were already updated. Greenbone says Rapid7 published a working proof of concept for CVE-2026-123007 and reports no attacks; 3CX's advisory does not mention exploitation.
What to do: 3CX advises self-managed customers to install V20 Update 10, Build 20.0.10.1801, and until then to restrict access to the 3CX web port (HTTPS) to the office, VPN or known IP addresses.
CVEs: CVE-2026-123633, CVE-2026-123007 (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: CISA advisory: Danfoss AK-SM 8xxA stack-based buffer overflow, CVE-2026-129713, CVSS v3.1 9.8
item.description:
CISA published an ICS advisory on 24 November on a stack-based buffer overflow in an unauthenticated CGI handler of Danfoss AK-SM 8xxA, version 5.4.0 and earlier (CVE-2026-129713, CVSS v3.1 9.8). The advisory says no known public exploitation has been reported to CISA and no patch is available; Danfoss plans a fix in an upcoming 5.5.x release.
What to do: CISA advises minimising network exposure, keeping control systems off the internet and behind firewalls, and using updated VPNs for remote access; Danfoss plans to fix this in AK-SM 800A software 5.5.x.
CVEs: CVE-2026-129713 (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: Broadcom's VMSA-2026-0011 fixes 23 vulnerabilities across VMware products, including ESX and vCenter
item.description:
Broadcom published advisory VMSA-2026-0011 on 24 November, fixing 23 vulnerabilities in VMware products. Rapid7 says CVE-2026-123903, a vCenter authentication bypass, has a Broadcom CVSSv3.1 score of 9.8 and a public proof-of-concept exploit that Rapid7 validated; it knows of no public reports of exploitation. ThaiCERT says Broadcom has not confirmed exploitation of these flaws.
What to do: Rapid7 advises urgent remediation outside normal patching cycles; apply the fixed versions in Broadcom's VMSA-2026-0011 (7.0: contact Broadcom support). ThaiCERT, citing Broadcom KB463535, suggests limiting the IOFilterVP port to the vCenter Server on ESXi 8.x meanwhile.
CVEs: CVE-2026-123910, CVE-2026-123911, CVE-2026-123903 (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: Cybernews reports POS terminals infected via old Windows flaw CVE-2024-49138, data of at least a million bank cards stolen
item.description:
Cybernews researchers report that hundreds of POS terminals in many countries, most in Brazil, were infected and that data of at least a million bank cards was stolen. Per the reports, attackers used CVE-2024-49138, a Windows Common Log File System driver flaw that Microsoft fixed in December 2024, to gain higher privileges and then installed a remote access trojan. Detik says exploit code for the flaw is public. The attackers are not named.
What to do: General advice: confirm that point-of-sale Windows systems have Microsoft's December 2024 fix for CVE-2024-49138, as the reports say it has been available since then.
CVEs: CVE-2024-49138 (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: GreyNoise reports GT13 intrusion campaign against Check Point Security Management Servers affecting at least 22 organisations
item.description:
GreyNoise says an actor it tracks as GT13 used 99 IP addresses against Check Point Security Management Servers, with confirmed attack activity between October 17th and November 2nd, 2026, impacting at least 22 distinct organizations globally. GreyNoise says the actor obtained data stolen from 24 distinct servers, and it believes the actor used agentic tooling. It does not attribute GT13 to any known group.
What to do: Check Point advises installing its jumbo hotfix for CVE-2026-16232 (July 2026), limiting Trusted Clients (GUI clients) to trusted IP addresses and restricting Management access to trusted IP addresses.
CVEs: CVE-2026-16232, CVE-2026-61500 (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: iTerm2 3.7.9 fixes command execution via crafted files displayed in the terminal; researcher publishes proof of concept
item.description:
iTerm2's 3.7.9 release notes, built on 20 November, say it fixes a security issue where a crafted file displayed in the terminal, for example with cat, could run arbitrary commands by abusing the Kitty image and drag-and-drop protocols. Researcher Minseong Kim of NSHC Red Alert Labs, credited by iTerm2, lists versions 3.6.1 – 3.7.8 as affected with default settings and has published proof-of-concept exploit code.
What to do: Update iTerm2 to 3.7.9, which iTerm2's release notes say fixes the issue; Cyber Security News also advises not printing raw contents of unfamiliar files into iTerm2 until then. (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: Norway's NSM says an unknown actor went after secrets in Azure API Management; Equinor and Skagerak Energi among affected
item.description:
Norway's NSM says an unknown actor actively went after access tokens, secrets and named values in Azure API Management, naming Equinor and Skagerak Energi among those affected. Techzine, relaying Microsoft, reports Microsoft found the flaw on 18 November and blocked the access on 19 November; the fix does not automatically invalidate credentials used earlier, and v2 tiers were not affected.
What to do: NSM advises assuming all secrets and named values are compromised and rotating all tokens and secrets; Microsoft advises changing potentially compromised credentials, monitoring systems they reach and reviewing logs. Check RuntimeVersion against NSM's thresholds; contact NSM on signs of compromise. (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: Unpatched ASP.NET anti-CSRF library Idunno.AntiCsrf flaw CVE-2026-131914 exploited, Mandiant says
item.description:
Mandiant's advisory says CVE-2026-131914 (CVSS 9.3), an insecure deserialization flaw in the legacy ASP.NET module Idunno.AntiCsrf version 0.9.1.0 / 0.9.1 Beta, is being exploited: "Active exploitation in the wild has been observed." According to Mandiant, the project is defunct, with no active maintainer or official patch. SecurityWeek reports that CISA added the flaw to its KEV catalog and that watchTowr saw exploit probes in its honeypots.
What to do: Mandiant advises organizations to discontinue use of Idunno.AntiCsrf (Idunno.AntiCsrf.dll) and replace it with an actively supported anti-CSRF alternative, and to audit Web.config files and bin/ directories for references to it.
CVEs: CVE-2026-131914 (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: CISA adds SAP NetWeaver flaw CVE-2025-42884 to its known-exploited catalog
item.description:
CISA's alert of 20 November lists SAP NetWeaver CVE-2025-42884 among four vulnerabilities added to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, based on evidence of active exploitation. Heise reports the flaw is a JNDI injection in NetWeaver Enterprise Portal, rated CVSS 6.5, that SAP fixed in its November 2025 Patchday.
What to do: General advice: confirm SAP NetWeaver Enterprise Portal has the fix SAP released in its November 2025 Patchday.
CVEs: CVE-2025-42884 (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: KEPCO says personal data of over one and a half million people leaked from its customer and procurement systems
item.description:
KEPCO said on 22 November it confirmed on 20 November a leak from Hanjeon ON and the SRM procurement system: 1,520,248 people by simple sum (Newsis), overlap unchecked (Dailian). Exposed: ID, bank account and card numbers. Dailian says KEPCO presumes an outside attacker. SBS reports a hacker offered KEPCO customer data on Telegram at 500 won per record; KEPCO told SBS the data being sold is from this attack.
What to do: KEPCO urges caution with calls, texts and emails that impersonate KEPCO or come from unclear sources; on 25 November it said affected customers get free security services and compensation for financial fraud under its terms (Newsis). (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: Poland's ePUAP e-government platform restricted after cyberattack; full operation restored 19 November, COI says
item.description:
Poland’s COI told Sekurak it preventively restricted access to part of the ePUAP system from 10 November, that the attack was detected and stopped, and that full operation returned on 19 November. Deputy PM Krzysztof Gawkowski said the attack came from abroad and that logs showed preparatory activity for a December operation against public administration. COI says the ABW is investigating and it found no sign of spread.
What to do: No action needed; for awareness. (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: ZOZO: about 15.18 million ZOZOTOWN customers' data leaked via PLAID KARTE breach
item.description:
ZOZO said on 20 November that customer information it managed on PLAID's KARTE leaked. About 15.18 million ZOZOTOWN customers incl. former members (member ID, age, gender, postal code) are affected, about 47,000 of them also with login name, email and phone number; about 13.93 million WEAR by ZOZO customers; about 24,000 brand staff. Passwords are not managed in KARTE; card data is not confirmed leaked.
What to do: ZOZO customers: be wary of phishing emails, texts or calls impersonating ZOZO, and do not open their links or attachments, as ZOZO advises. (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: SMBC says up to about 14 million customer records leaked via PLAID KARTE breach
item.description:
SMBC said on 20 November that up to about 14 million records of customer information leaked after unauthorized access to KARTE, a service from its contractor PLAID. The data is dates of birth, category values for age band, gender and whether a phone number is registered, and notice flags; SMBC says it is not linked to names and cannot identify individuals. No impact on assets or transactions is confirmed so far.
What to do: SMBC says it will never ask for passwords or card details by email or phone about this; it urges customers not to open links or attachments in suspicious messages claiming to be from the bank. (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: Marui Group: about 8.83 million and about 8.5 million customer records leaked via PLAID KARTE breach
item.description:
Marui Group said on 20 November that customer data leaked after unauthorized access to PLAID's KARTE, which it says came from PLAID's system, not Marui's. About 8.83 million people (name, gender, date of birth, email, customer management number) and about 8.5 million EPOS CARD users incl. former members (customer management number, gender) are affected; about 60,000 of them may also have name, age, annual income and cash-advance limit exposed. Card numbers are not confirmed leaked.
What to do: Marui and EPOS CARD customers: be careful with suspicious emails and do not open URLs in them or enter personal information, as Marui Group advises. (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: Amazon: attackers used the Cairn AI tool to exploit a MONAI Label zero-day and take over a server, BleepingComputer reports
item.description:
Amazon found AI agents running the Cairn tool exploiting a path traversal zero-day in MONAI Label, a medical imaging application, within 11 minutes of mapping its API, BleepingComputer reports. They gained root on a server. Amazon attributes it to a Chinese-nexus actor with moderate confidence. Minuto da Segurança (25 Nov) says advisory GHSA-qc22-rmgc-vg94 is fixed in version 0.8.6.
What to do: Minuto da Segurança advises updating MONAI Label to 0.8.6 after testing, not exposing the server directly to the internet, and checking exposed instances for unexpected files such as sitecustomize.py.
CVEs: CVE-2026-133968 (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: Mitel fixes 5 MiCollab AWV flaws, two critical; Italy's CSIRT relays the advisory
item.description:
Mitel advisory MISA-2026-0012 fixes 5 flaws in the AWV component of MiCollab release 10.3 (10.3.0.18) and earlier, and CISA added all five to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 25 November. Securitylab.ru, relaying an Accenture APEX Labs investigation, says attacks began before fixes were available and in one case reached the domain controller 32 minutes after the attack began; it says experts suspect part of the attack was automated with AI.
What to do: Mitel advises applying its patch for release 10.3 (10.3.0.18) per KB000129195 or upgrading, and restricting external access to AWV if it cannot be patched promptly; CISA requires vendor-instructed mitigations and evaluating internet exposure.
CVEs: CVE-2026-133275, CVE-2026-133303, CVE-2026-133311, CVE-2026-133323, CVE-2026-133324 (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: React2STEAL: GitHub Actions scanners exploit React2Shell and publish stolen secrets
item.description:
OpenSourceMalware published research on November 18 on a campaign it named React2STEAL: 45 GitHub repositories across 44 accounts run scanners for React2Shell (CVE-2025-55182) and CVE-2025-29927 and commit results to public repositories. It found at least 1,281 victim hostnames across about 1,100 domains. It lists the actor as unknown. GitGuardian's write-up says patches for both flaws have been available for months.
What to do: OpenSourceMalware advises: upgrade React and Next.js to fixed versions; until then strip or reject the x-middleware-subrequest header at the proxy or WAF, check logs for it and for /_next/image requests aimed at the metadata address, rotate exposed secrets, and enforce IMDSv2.
CVEs: CVE-2025-55182, CVE-2025-29927 (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: Huntress: attackers exploit ScreenConnect flaw CVE-2026-84869 against MSP technicians' workstations
item.description:
Huntress reports attackers exploiting CVE-2026-84869 in ScreenConnect, which lets a guest push files that run on a technician's machine. It saw one full compromise of an MSP technician workstation on November 12 and, since October 20, at least 688,000 guest 'run file' requests for update*.bat hitting 42 MSP servers from 29 IP addresses. Huntress recommends updating technician host clients to 26.6.5 or later; updating the server alone does not fix it.
What to do: Update every technician's ScreenConnect host client to 26.6.5 or later; if you cannot, remove the TransferFiles permission from roles and session groups, as ConnectWise advises, and check Session.db for guest RanFiles or SentFiles events.
CVEs: CVE-2026-84869 (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: Santos port authority systems still partly down after 6 November outage and cyber intrusion; Federal Police investigating
item.description:
Santos Port Authority (APS) systems went down on 6 November. Gazeta do Povo (13 November) reports a Federal Police inquiry opened on 10 November and that hackers emailed APS seeking contact, unanswered. APS's own 17 November notice says a power outage shut its datacentres, then an intrusion erased data; cargo handling was never compromised. ABC do ABC (18 November) says more than 30 systems still run alternatively and APS says no confidential data leaked.
What to do: General advice: port users and shippers should rely only on channels announced by the Autoridade Portuária de Santos, and treat unexpected emails or calls about cargo, access or payments with caution. (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: Google: ARMORY CASTLE exploits vCenter zero-day CVE-2026-123890 in espionage campaign
item.description:
Google Threat Intelligence Group says ARMORY CASTLE, a suspected PRC-nexus espionage actor it formerly tracked as UNC5221, exploited CVE-2026-123890, an unauthenticated SRP session key disclosure flaw in VMware vCenter Server, from early September 2026. SecurityWeek reports a CVSS of 9.8 and fixes in vCenter 8.0 U3m, 9.0.2.0200 and 9.1.1.0200, with no public patch for 7.0. Google names no victims.
What to do: Google advises applying Broadcom's patches immediately; SecurityWeek lists fixed vCenter builds 8.0 U3m, 9.0.2.0200 and 9.1.1.0200 and says 7.0 has no public patch. Google also advises restricting inbound access to and egress from vCenter, as described in its post.
CVEs: CVE-2026-123890, CVE-2026-102764 (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: Cisco Expressway clustering flaw CVE-2026-76466 exploited after public PoC, F6 reports
item.description:
Cisco's critical advisory (CVSS 9.8) says an unauthenticated remote attacker can run commands as root on clustered Expressway-C and Expressway-E. SecurityWeek reports F6 investigated an attack on two internet-exposed X15.5.3 devices that spread to two cluster nodes after a GitHub PoC; Security Affairs says the victim was a Russian organization. CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 20 November, Help Net Security reports. Fix: X15.5.20.
What to do: If you run clustered Expressway, upgrade to X15.5.20 or later now (X14 and earlier must move to a fixed release; Cisco says no workaround). If you cannot patch at once, F6 advises restricting TCP 4371-4372 at the firewall to trusted cluster node IPs.
CVEs: CVE-2026-76466 (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: SonicWall: retire Gen 6 firewalls now, no more patches even for critical flaws
item.description:
SonicWall's advisory of 18 November says every Gen 6 and Gen 6.5 firewall running SonicOS 6.x, including NSv, has reached end of support and will get no firmware or security patches regardless of severity. SonicWall says it expects internet-facing Gen 6 units to be actively targeted and tells customers to replace them with Gen 8. No new CVE is named.
What to do: Inventory every Gen 6 unit; replace internet-facing ones first; meanwhile disable WAN management and SSL VPN (or restrict sources), enforce MFA, and monitor logs. (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: N-able says attackers accessed a Mail Assure and SpamExperts cloud server
item.description:
N-able says unknown actors accessed one server in its hosted Mail Assure and SpamExperts cloud, and it found no evidence customer data was compromised. N-able told SecurityWeek exploitation was confined to a single hosted server and the impacted functionality is restored. Per The Hacker News, a separate SSRF flaw, CVE-2026-134624 (CVSS 4.0 score 9.3), was found during the investigation; N-able has not said whether it was the way in.
What to do: As The Hacker News reports N-able's advisory, SpamExperts Local Cloud operators should confirm they run build 20261121.1943; Hosted Cloud users have nothing to install. The Hacker News says N-able revoked customers' existing API tokens and reset local users' passwords.
CVEs: CVE-2026-134624 (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: WordPress 7.1.5 security release fixes unauthenticated privilege escalation and SQL injection
item.description:
WordPress 7.1.5, released November 18, is a security release; Patchstack counts twenty fixes. They include unauthenticated privilege escalation through Template Part block attributes that the project says could lead to remote code execution, two SQL injections, a Multisite Super Admin takeover and stored XSS in comments. The project recommends updating immediately and its post does not mention exploitation.
What to do: WordPress.org recommends updating your sites immediately (Dashboard > Updates > Update Now); sites with automatic background updates will update automatically. (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: Bulgaria says hackers had access to government networks for about five years
item.description:
Bulgaria's digital minister Ivan Vassilev said that since 2021 more than 130 GB, or 62 million pages, of documents had been downloaded from state networks. Per Reuters, several international hacking groups are believed responsible, with no conclusive foreign-government link. Fakti.bg reported on 25 November that China's embassy sent a protest note to parliament over MP Bozhidar Bozhanov's remark that Beijing-linked groups could be behind it; he said attribution is for the executive.
What to do: No action needed; for awareness. General advice: government and critical-sector defenders should review document-exchange systems for long-dwell access and centralise monitoring. (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: DHC: about 19.11 million customer records leaked via PLAID KARTE breach
item.description:
DHC announced on November 18 that about 19.11 million online-shop customer records leaked after unauthorized access to PLAID's KARTE marketing service; Business+IT says PLAID told DHC of the intrusion on November 13. Leaked items include names, email addresses and dates of birth; login passwords and card payment data were not included, and DHC says no misuse has been confirmed. DHC plans to report jointly with PLAID to Japan's Personal Information Protection Commission.
What to do: General advice: DHC customers should treat unexpected emails or texts using your name and birth date as phishing; change reused passwords. (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: Rakuten Securities second report: leaked customer data includes names, addresses and phone numbers
item.description:
Rakuten Securities said on 17 November that a third party may have accessed its systems. Its second report of 24 November, relayed by Impress Watch, says about 4.41 million records include names and addresses; J-CAST says about 1.19 million belong to people who had not opened an account, and the company told J-CAST it is investigating why. No password or PIN leak was confirmed.
What to do: Rakuten Securities, as reported by SBbit, recommends setting up passkey authentication and says it will not put URLs in emails about this incident or phone to ask for personal or login information. (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: Chile's Huatacondo solar plant still offline almost three months after cyberattack recorded by grid operator
item.description:
Chile's Coordinador Eléctrico Nacional recorded the forced disconnection of the 103 MW Huatacondo solar plant and its 98 MW/312 MWh battery system on 27 August with the cause 'cyberattack'; its 14 November report still showed both at 0% availability. The Coordinador says an investigation remains ongoing. Tarapacá's regional energy secretary told La Estrella de Iquique, relayed by Emol, the plant stays disconnected for the owner's reasons. No technical cause or reconnection date is public.
What to do: General advice: operators of solar, storage and thermal plants should confirm that remote access paths and telecontrol are monitored and that their incident-reporting steps are rehearsed. (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: Drupal reports core flaw CVE-2026-132165 exploited on live sites; fixed in 10.6.22, 11.3.22 and 11.4.13
item.description:
Drupal rates SA-CORE-2026-017, CVE-2026-132165, highly critical: under specific conditions install.php can be used to reinstall a site, leading to takeover or code execution. Drupal's advisory update says it received a report of exploitation on live sites as early as 2026-11-19 19:00 UTC. Fixed in 10.6.22, 11.3.22 and 11.4.13. CISA added CVE-2026-132165 to its known-exploited catalog on 24 November. NSFOCUS (27 November) says a proof of concept is publicly available.
What to do: Drupal advises updating core to 10.6.22, 11.3.22 or 11.4.13; if you cannot upgrade, secure the installer as Drupal describes. Older branches are end of life, per Drupal.
CVEs: CVE-2026-132165, CVE-2026-132166 (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: CISA adds four exploited flaws to KEV: Synology DSM, LiteLLM, Apache Axis, REDCap
item.description:
CISA added four vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on November 18, citing evidence of active exploitation: CVE-2024-10441 in Synology DiskStation Manager, CVE-2026-40217 in BerriAI LiteLLM (unprotected alternate channel), CVE-2026-90436 in Apache Axis (unsafe reflection) and CVE-2026-90817 in Vanderbilt University REDCap (code injection). The alert gives no fixed versions. The Hacker News reports exploitation including ransomware on Synology NAS, cryptomining and LLMjacking.
What to do: CISA directs federal agencies to remediate under BOD 26-04: find Synology DSM, LiteLLM, Apache Axis and REDCap in your environment and apply vendor fixes where they exist. The Hacker News reports Axis 1.x is end of life and unpatched, and names migrating or applying the July 12, 2026 commit as options.
CVEs: CVE-2024-10441, CVE-2026-40217, CVE-2026-90436, CVE-2026-90817 (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: SANS honeypots see scans for chained LiteLLM and Starlette flaws (CVE-2026-42271, CVE-2026-48710)
item.description:
SANS ISC honeypots recorded requests to /mcp-rest/test/tools/list attempting to chain CVE-2026-42271 in LiteLLM with CVE-2026-48710 in Starlette for unauthenticated remote code execution. Starlette before 1.0.1 does not validate the Host header. SANS cites a Horizon3.ai write-up on the chain and says exploitation was reported in July. Whether any attempts succeeded is not stated.
What to do: SANS advises defending against the underlying vulnerability, validating hostnames, reducing attack surface and patching; Starlette 1.0.1 is the version that validates the Host header. The page gives no LiteLLM fix version.
CVEs: CVE-2026-42271, CVE-2026-48710 (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: CERT-FR: NGINX flaws allow unauthenticated remote code execution over HTTP/2; public PoC exists
item.description:
CERT-FR warns that two flaws in F5 NGINX, CVE-2026-123633 and CVE-2026-123007, allow unauthenticated remote code execution over HTTP/2; a public proof of concept exists for CVE-2026-123007. Fixed in Open Source 1.31.9 and 1.30.7. Palo Alto Networks says PAN-OS and Panorama with HTTP/2 enabled are affected and it is not aware of malicious exploitation. Disabling HTTP/2 is an interim workaround for those two flaws.
What to do: CERT-FR recommends applying F5's fixes (bulletins K000163926 and K000163928; Open Source 1.30.7 or 1.31.9) and, until patched, disabling HTTP/2, which covers only the HTTP/2 flaws. Palo Alto Networks says PAN-OS and Panorama customers can disable the HTTP/2 option.
CVEs: CVE-2026-123633, CVE-2026-123007, CVE-2026-123634, CVE-2026-121810, CVE-2026-113425 (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: Microsoft Agent Framework PyPI package compromised with credential stealer
item.description:
Versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 of the agent-framework package on PyPI were published on November 17 with a credential stealer that runs when Python starts, targeting cloud, GitHub and AI credentials and tokens. PyPI quarantined both; 1.26.0 is the last safe version. Italy's CSIRT (ACN) says the malware installed no OS-level persistence and downloaded no further payloads. Xakep.ru reports Microsoft said it made some repositories private during the investigation; the entry route is unknown.
What to do: Wiz and CSIRT Italia advise pinning agent-framework to 1.26.0, checking lockfiles, CI logs and environments for 1.26.1 or 1.26.2, and rotating credentials and tokens exposed to any host that installed them. (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: Apache warns Roller RCE flaw (CVE-2026-129448) is exploited in attacks
item.description:
Apache says an unauthenticated remote code execution flaw in Roller, CVE-2026-129448, is being exploited. It is a deserialization bug in the XML-RPC interface affecting versions 4.0.0 through 6.1.4, and is the same bug as CVE-2026-82384, which named only 6.1.5. Version 6.1.6 or later fixes it. Italy's CSIRT (ACN) reported active exploitation on 23 November.
What to do: Apache advises upgrading Roller to 6.1.6 or later. If you cannot, Apache says to set enabledForExtensions to false in WEB-INF/web.xml or remove the /roller-services/xmlrpc servlet mapping, then restart Roller; switching off XML-RPC in the admin UI is not enough.
CVEs: CVE-2026-129448 (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: NCSC Netherlands: public exploit code for critical Ivanti Endpoint Manager flaw (CVE-2026-121653)
item.description:
The Dutch National Cyber Security Centre warns that proof-of-concept code is now public for CVE-2026-121653, an SQL injection flaw in the Core of Ivanti Endpoint Manager before 2024 SU8. A remote attacker without credentials can use it to run code. A second flaw, CVE-2026-18128, lets an attacker positioned on the network read and alter agent traffic sent in clear text. Ivanti has released updates.
What to do: Install the updates Ivanti has released for Endpoint Manager, as the NCSC-NL advisory advises; see Ivanti's November 2026 security advisory for affected versions and fixes.
CVEs: CVE-2026-121653, CVE-2026-18128 (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: Japan's RIKEN takes Fugaku supercomputer offline after intrusion
item.description:
RIKEN's first notice says an outside party reached Fugaku's internal operational network from November 10 to 13 through a public web page showing Fugaku's operational status; the exact method is under investigation. Its second notice (20 Nov) lists 4,222 Fugaku users as affected and says 430 credentials (233 SSH private keys without a passphrase, 197 with one) were exfiltrated; some were used for external connections. Fugaku stays offline; no attacker is named.
What to do: Fugaku users: revoke and replace SSH keys used with Fugaku, as RIKEN asks, and watch for phishing emails. Others: no action needed; for awareness. (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: Canadian Centre for Cyber Security: Microsoft November rollup AV26-1142 updated for exploited flaw CVE-2026-124194
item.description:
Cyber Centre advisory AV26-1142 relays Microsoft's November 2026 security updates to Canadian organisations. The affected list spans Windows 10 and 11, Windows Server 2012 to 2025, Microsoft 365 Apps and Office, Exchange Server Subscription Edition, SharePoint Server, SQL Server, .NET, Visual Studio and many Azure services. Update 1, dated November 12, adds that Microsoft reports CVE-2026-124194 as exploited and that CISA catalogued it on November 10.
What to do: Install Microsoft's November 2026 security updates across Windows, Office, Exchange, SharePoint, SQL Server and developer tools, taking the fix for CVE-2026-124194 first. Use the MSRC release notes linked from the advisory to scope the work.
CVEs: CVE-2026-124194 (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: NCSC New Zealand alerts on OpenSSH 'SSHole' authentication bypass CVE-2026-123158
item.description:
New Zealand's NCSC issued an alert on November 11 about CVE-2026-123158, nicknamed SSHole, an authentication bypass in OpenSSH on Linux that may give an attacker root access. A system is exposed only if it runs a version before 10.6p2, uses musl libc, does not use PAM and accepts password logins. The alert does not say whether the flaw is being exploited.
What to do: Identify Linux systems running OpenSSH before 10.6p2 on musl libc without PAM that accept password logins, and update to 10.6p2. Until then, disable password authentication or turn SSH off on those systems.
CVEs: CVE-2026-123158 (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: CERT-EU rates Citrix NetScaler flaws critical: unauthenticated memory overflows scored up to 9.5
item.description:
CERT-EU Security Advisory 2026-020 covers 28 memory flaws in Citrix NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway. CVE-2026-120868, scored 9.3, sits in core packet processing and affects every deployment, default configuration included, without authentication. CVE-2026-107412, scored 9.5, affects appliances set up as a Gateway or AAA virtual server. Citrix reports no exploitation and no public proof of concept is confirmed.
What to do: Upgrade customer-managed NetScaler ADC and Gateway to 14.1-73.57 or 13.1-64.39, FIPS builds to 14.1-73.58 FIPS or 13.1-37.293. Do internet-facing Gateway and AAA appliances first.
CVEs: CVE-2026-120868, CVE-2026-107412 (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: Canadian Centre for Cyber Security: Check Point advisory AV26-1154 updated to note an exploited flaw
item.description:
Cyber Centre advisory AV26-1154, issued November 12 and updated the next day, covers two flaws across multiple versions of Check Point Force firewalls, management and log servers, Multi-Domain products and Maestro Orchestrator. It relays Check Point's statement that CVE-2026-123039, a local escalation to root, is being exploited in the wild. Update 1 records that CISA added that flaw to its exploited-vulnerabilities catalog on November 13.
What to do: Apply Check Point's fixes for CVE-2026-123039 and CVE-2026-107484 on firewalls, management and log servers, Multi-Domain servers and Maestro Orchestrator. Read the Check Point advisories and the CISA catalog entry linked from the advisory.
CVEs: CVE-2026-123039, CVE-2026-107484 (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: CSA Singapore warns of reported active exploitation of Apache HTTP Server mod_http2 flaw CVE-2026-119618
item.description:
Singapore's Cyber Security Agency issued alert AL-2026-164 on November 17 about CVE-2026-119618, rated 8.1, in Apache HTTP Server's mod_http2, affecting 2.4.55 up to but not including 2.4.71. The agency says exploitation is reportedly under way and proof-of-concept code is public. Apache lists it as critical and fixed in 2.4.71. Praetorian says a worker thread modifying a shared headers table is the cause, and it has no working remote code execution exploit yet.
What to do: As CSA urges, update affected Apache HTTP Server installations (2.4.55 to before 2.4.71 with mod_http2 enabled) to the latest version immediately; the Apache advisory lists 2.4.71 as the fixed release.
CVEs: CVE-2026-119618 (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: CISA adds exploited Perforce Puppet Enterprise flaw (CVE-2026-115731) to KEV
item.description:
CISA added CVE-2026-115731, a deserialization flaw in Perforce Puppet Enterprise, to its KEV catalog on November 17, citing active exploitation; Help Net Security says federal agencies must fix it by December 1. It reports a client holding a Puppet CA-signed certificate can send a crafted report and run code as the Puppet Server user. Fixed in 2026.0.1, 2025.12.1 and 2023.8.13.
What to do: Perforce advises upgrading Puppet Enterprise to 2026.0.1, 2025.12.1 or 2023.8.13 (Puppet Core 9.1.3 or 8.22.2), restarting the server as soon as possible, and reviewing autosign configuration as a temporary mitigation, per Help Net Security.
CVEs: CVE-2026-115731 (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: Dragos counts 1,266 ransomware incidents at industrial organisations in Q3 2026
item.description:
Dragos recorded 1,266 ransomware incidents affecting industrial organisations in the third quarter of 2026, up 11% from 1,140 the quarter before. Manufacturing took 69% of them and the United States 37%. According to Dragos, Qilin led with 195 incidents, ahead of The Gentlemen (167 claimed victims) and Cl0p (35). Dragos names exploited edge devices and enterprise applications, and stolen VPN credentials, among the ways in. Dragos saw no operator directly manipulate an industrial control system.
What to do: Dragos recommends rotating administrator and VPN credentials, especially on FortiGate appliances, enforcing MFA on all remote access, auditing for administrator accounts not created internally, and patching edge devices rapidly.
CVEs: CVE-2026-0257, CVE-2026-15409, CVE-2026-15410, CVE-2026-63077, CVE-2026-59310, CVE-2026-12569 (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)

item.title: Rapid7 and CISA: critical Java flaw CVE-2026-114938 (Java4Shell) in Java 17 and later; Oracle patches released
item.description:
Rapid7 and CISA warn of CVE-2026-114938 (Java4Shell), a memory corruption bug in the x86-64 HotSpot JVM Base64 decoder that could allow remote code execution; Oracle released fixes on November 17. SecurityWeek (Nov 19) reports GreyNoise saw over 150 matching requests from five IP addresses, with no successful intrusions seen on its sensors; Cisco, Siemens, Elastic and Red Hat issued advisories.
What to do: Inventory every Java runtime, including bundled ones, and install the fixed releases (for example 17.0.21.1, 21.0.13.1, 25.0.5.1, 27.0.1.1), internet-facing systems first. See Rapid7's advisory for compensating controls where patching is not possible.
CVEs: CVE-2026-114938 (Written by CyberView AI (a Claude model).)
